name: Assam
tagline: The Land of Red River and Blue Hills
description: Famed for its world-renowned Assam tea, the mighty Brahmaputra river, rich biodiversity in Kaziranga and Manas, and exquisite Muga silk traditions.
permit_details: No Inner Line Permit (ILP) required for Indian or foreign nationals.

name: Arunachal Pradesh
description: India's easternmost frontier blessed with snow-capped Himalayan peaks, pristine river valleys, ancient Monpa monasteries, and vibrant tribal cultures.
permit_details: Inner Line Permit (ILP) is required for Indian citizens (available online). Foreign tourists require a Protected Area Permit (PAP).
highlights: Ziro Valley Pine Groves & Apatani Culture

name: Meghalaya
description: A highland wonderland of living root bridges, mystical limestone caves, cascading plunges like Nohkalikai, and sacred groves protected by Khasi, Jaintia, and Garo clans.
permit_details: No Inner Line Permit required for Indian or international tourists.
highlights: Double Decker Living Root Bridge in Cherrapunji
Crystal clear Umngot River at Dawki

name: Manipur
description: Home to the world's only floating national park on Loktak Lake, the classical Manipuri Raas Leela dance, polo birthplace, and the matriarchal Ima Keithel market.
permit_details: Inner Line Permit (ILP) required for domestic Indian travellers (obtained online or at arrival counters).

name: Mizoram
description: Characterized by rolling bamboo hills, pristine cloudscapes, warm community camaraderie, vibrant handloom shawls, and rhythmic Cheraw bamboo dances.
permit_details: Inner Line Permit (ILP) required for domestic visitors. Available online or at Lengpui Airport.

name: Nagaland
description: A rugged paradise of 16 recognized indigenous tribes, heroic warrior folklore, emerald rolling valleys like Dzukou, and the world-famous Hornbill Festival.
permit_details: Inner Line Permit (ILP) is required for domestic travellers. Foreign nationals must register with the local FRRO.
best_season: October to May (December for Hornbill Festival)
highlights: Hornbill Festival at Kisama Heritage Village

name: Tripura
description: Rich in royal history with the gleaming white Ujjayanta and floating Neermahal palaces, alongside mystical rock-cut sculptures at Unakoti and Debtamura.
permit_details: No Inner Line Permit required for Indian or foreign travellers.
highlights: Neermahal Water Palace on Rudrasagar Lake

name: Sikkim
tagline: Valley of Rice and Sacred Peaks
description: An eco-haven cradled beneath Mount Kangchenjunga (8,586m) boasting sacred alpine lakes, ancient Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, and vibrant rhododendron valleys.
permit_details: No ILP for Indian citizens for general entry. Special permits required for Nathu La, Tsomgo Lake, Gurudongmar, and North Sikkim borders.
best_season: March to May & October to mid-December
